call_points.text: Total projects on hand are ₹2,800 Cr, with about ₹1,500 Cr more to be spent over the next two years.
Weak nitric acid plant is about three months delayed, which management says will be recouped; AMUGL and AN Melt are online.
TGU production is expected at broadly last year's level; TGU was one of the significant contributors to Q1 profit.
Cash on hand is around ₹4,000 Cr, held across G-Sec, GSFS and bank deposits.
Oil and gas prices rose in Q1 on the Middle East crisis and remain volatile; gas availability is a concern though operations are unaffected.
Management declined to give Q2 realisation guidance, citing a volatile market, and said it has never given such guidance.
GNFC proposed an MoU with GMDC for underground coal gasification; studies are ongoing and an announcement is expected soon.
Ammonium nitrate, weak nitric acid and ammonia expansion are on track, with weak nitric acid delayed about 2.5 months.
All three projects (ammonia expansion, nitric acid, ammonium nitrate melt) are to come up by next year; CCPP operational by Q2.
CCPP saving potential maintained at ₹10-12 Cr per month, expected to accrue from H2FY27.
Chemical realisations rose 6% to 28% product to product QoQ, with formic acid the exception.
Ammonium nitrate prices improved 20% QoQ and are sustaining at higher levels; imports are low on the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Aniline stays unviable standalone against Chinese dumping; GNFC does job work on a fixed margin instead of expanding.
Urea energy norms are under approval and fixed cost revision at discussion stage; management sees almost no chance of a urea turnaround until then.
High gas prices make methanol production unviable; GNFC is weighing buying methanol or acetic acid for downstream ethyl acetate.
No buyback is on the table; the board declared a 210% dividend, ₹21 per share, the second highest in its 50-year history.
The earlier planned JV with INEOS has become a licensing dialogue for additional capacity.

CCPP saving potential of ₹10-12 Cr per month, expected to accrue from H2FY27.
Ammonia expansion, nitric acid and ammonium nitrate melt projects are all to come up by next year (FY28).
Completed projects expected to add revenue of ₹1,200-1,500 Cr and contribution of ₹500-600 Cr
FY27 capex targeted at ₹1,200-1,500 Cr for the rest of the year, ₹1,500-1,800 Cr for the full year
TGU production expected broadly at last year's level

industry: Commodities > Chemicals > Chemicals & Petrochemicals > Commodity Chemicals

operating_notes.text: FY26 production: ammonia oil route close to 3 lakh MT, gas route 360,000 MT, CNA 147,000 MT, WNA about 430,000 MT, TDI about 57,000 MT, formic acid close to 34,000 MT and AN Melt close to 170,000 MT.
TGU output exceeded 210,000 MT in FY26 against a 169,000 MT average capacity, with production doubled in March 2026 at the cost of neem urea.
Acetic acid and most plants ran above 100% utilisation while TDI ran close to 80%, in line with the global operating factor.
Q1FY27 ammonia production was about 173,000 t, 54% from the oil route and 49% from gas as stated.
Dahej steam saving estimated at ₹30,000-40,000 per tonne of TDI at current gas and coal prices.
GNFC (n)Code business is around ₹100 Cr in size and sits within the 'other' segment.
